author: Fixture Reporter
content:
Nvidia's sales are increasingly concentrated among a few buyers. Three direct customers supplied 44%, or $78.2 billion, of its $177.8 billion revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027. A year earlier, two customers represented 35%.

CFO Colette Kress described a neocloud approach that earns revenue both when hardware is sold and when its computing capacity is rented. Nvidia supplies data-center infrastructure to AI cloud operators and supports capacity financing through cloud-service agreements, then receives a portion of rental income generated by third-party use.

Data Center revenue climbed 117% year over year to $89 billion in the most recent quarter. Nvidia expects businesses outside the hyperscalers, including sovereign AI projects, regional neoclouds, enterprises, edge computing and air-gapped facilities, to account for roughly half of its Data Center business.

Commitments associated with the model stood at $36 billion on July 26. Agreements generally run for six years, and commitments decrease as third parties or Nvidia consume the capacity.

The strategy seeks to broaden the users of Nvidia compute and add recurring rental income to equipment sales. Utilization, revenue sharing and non-hyperscaler demand will help indicate whether it succeeds.
headline: Nvidia's Neocloud Model Adds Rental Revenue To GPU Sales As Customer Concentration Rises
summary: With three direct customers accounting for 44% of first-half fiscal 2027 revenue, Nvidia is pursuing hardware sales plus a share of compute rental income.
